plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs spill over with silky, open-faced blooms and golden stamens just as most gardens fade. Petals drop in soft drifts beneath the branches like pink confetti.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn to mid-winter, peaking in late autumn
plants.location: Japan, where it grows wild and in gardens
plants.funFact: Sasanqua leaves are close relatives of the tea plant's, and the seeds are pressed into camellia oil, used for centuries in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Street-lining trees erupt in clouds of lilac-blue trumpet flowers, carpeting pavements and parked cars in violet as the southern summer begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: November to December in Perth, Western Australia
plants.location: Perth, Western Australia, and other southern-hemisphere cities
plants.funFact: Native to South America, the jacaranda was planted widely across Australian cities, and a fall of its flowers is traditionally said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Schlumbergera × buckleyi
plants.description: Arching, leaf-like stems dangle with vivid tubular flowers, brightening windowsills and conservatories at the darkest time of the northern year.
plants.location: Brazil's coastal mountains (native range) and homes worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is a jungle plant, not a desert one: in the wild it perches on tree branches in humid Brazilian forests.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Tall shrubs in their native Mexico wear fiery crowns of colored bracts around tiny golden flower clusters called cyathia.
plants.location: Mexico, its native range, and warm gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The 'petals' are really modified leaves called bracts; the true flowers are the small yellow cups at the center.
